 HFCL Share Price in a 5% HFCL Lower Circuit on 9 November 2026, Down 21% in a Month: What Is Known After Record Q2 FY27 Profit and What Lies Ahead
 HFCL hit a 5% lower circuit on 9 Nov 2026, down about 21% in a month (Mint). Q2 FY27 profit was a record Rs 394.22 crore, up 448%; no source confirms the cause of the fall.
 Updated: 9 Nov 2026 • 12:47 pm
 Posted by: Chaitanya Auti 
 Quick Answer 
 The HFCL share price was locked in a 5% HFCL lower circuit on 9 November 2026 and is down about 21% in a month, per Mint, even though Q2 FY27 profit rose to a record Rs 394.22 crore. No source I found confirms the cause of the latest fall, so this article separates the facts from the guesses.
 The HFCL share price was locked in a 5% HFCL lower circuit on 9 November 2026, and Mint reports the stock is down about 21% in a month. That is a sharp turn for a company that posted its best-ever quarter only three weeks earlier. This article sets out the price snapshot, what the sources say about the fall, the Q2 FY27 numbers, valuation and a neutral checklist for what lies ahead. For the earlier slide in September, see our earlier HFCL fall-streak article .

 The HFCL share price trades in the BE series, which carries a 5% daily band, so an HFCL lower circuit stops the price from falling more than 5% in a session. MarketsMOJO's weekly review shows a different 6 November close of Rs 209.95 for the week ended 6 November, so the base behind the Rs 216.49 previous close on the Univest page does not match every source. Use a live quote on the HFCL Ltd page for the exact figure. The Rs 205.67 figure and Mint's 21% monthly fall are both time-stamped snapshots, not live quotes.
 Why Is the HFCL Share Price Falling? What Is Known and What Is Not 
 Possible reason for the HFCL lower circuit 
 Evidence found 
 Status 
 Run of lower circuits before the HFCL lower circuit on 9 November 
 MarketsMOJO shows lower circuits on 2, 5 and 6 November, an upper circuit near Rs 228.16 on 4 November, and a week that closed down 9.23% at Rs 209.95 
 Reported; cause for 9 November not stated 
 Rating downgrade 
 MarketsMOJO moved its own rating to Hold on 2 November, the day of a lower circuit near Rs 219.73 
 A third-party rating, not a company event 
 Telecom sector weakness 
 Equitymaster cited a 1.27% fall in the BSE Telecom index on 5 November as a possible reason 
 Possible factor; not confirmed for 9 November 
 Earlier HFCL lower circuit days 
 Lower circuits on 9 October (3.26% band) and 15 October (5% band, near Rs 243.82) 
 Fact; shows the stock was already volatile 
 Profit-taking after the record quarter 
 Stock hit a 5% upper circuit on 19 October and has since fallen about 23.5% 
 My reading; no source states the cause 
 Company news 
 Subsidiary HFCL Connectivity Systems was formed on 22 October 2026 
 Fact; not linked to the fall by any source 
 I could not find a company statement, exchange filing or news report that explains the 9 November HFCL lower circuit. Mint's headline asks what lies ahead, and the honest answer starts with that gap. When a stock locks in an HFCL-style lower circuit, sellers outnumber buyers at the price floor, and the HFCL lower circuit has now repeated several times in a month. Whether the HFCL lower circuit reflects selling pressure, sector weakness or a technical break below the moving averages cannot be proved from public data.

 For the first half of FY27, revenue was Rs 4,456.77 crore, up 132.81%, and profit after tax was Rs 639.86 crore. Management said it expects revenue growth of at least 80% in FY27 and called Q2 its best-ever quarter, per press reports of the results. That is company guidance, not a forecast by Univest. The numbers explain the 19 October upper circuit, but they do not explain why an HFCL lower circuit followed and the HFCL share price has since fallen, because results are already in the price once a market has digested them.

 The lower P/E is mostly the arithmetic of a bigger trailing profit, since the earnings in the denominator rose sharply after Q2. MarketsMOJO noted the stock trading below all its moving averages in its weekly review, which differs from the Univest page, where the 200-day average sits below the price. The two views use different dates and data vendors, so check a live chart. A stock that sits below its 50-day average but above its 200-day average is in a short-term downtrend within a longer-term uptrend, which is a description and not a signal.
 What Lies Ahead After the HFCL Lower Circuit: A Neutral Checklist for the HFCL Share Price 
 Investor situation 
 Questions to consider 
 Existing holder 
 What is my average cost against Rs 205.67, how large is the position, and can I sit through more lower circuits if sellers stay in control? 
 New buyer 
 Does the 38.25 P/E suit my view of a contract-driven telecom equipment business, and have I read the Q2 filing myself? 
 Short-term trader 
 In a 5% band, an HFCL lower circuit can lock the exit; do I accept that an HFCL share price position may be impossible to sell on a bad day? 
 Long-term investor 
 Do the Rs 28,900 crore order book and the 80% growth guidance match my own execution checks? 
 Things worth watching include whether the HFCL lower circuit repeats and the HFCL share price keeps hitting the 5% band, whether volumes dry up, any exchange filing that explains the move, and the telecom index. A rally in the HFCL share price on its own, like the 19 October jump, says little about the next session. The company's order execution and margins across the next two quarters will matter more than a single week's price action.
 Conclusion 
 The HFCL share price hit its 5% HFCL lower circuit on 9 November 2026, about 23.5% below the 19 October upper circuit, even though Q2 FY27 profit of Rs 394.22 crore was a record. The cause of the latest HFCL lower circuit is unconfirmed. Check a live quote, read the exchange filings and consult a SEBI-registered adviser before acting.

 Frequently Asked Questions on the HFCL Share Price 
 What caused the HFCL lower circuit in the HFCL share price? 
 Ans. Mint reported on 9 November 2026 that HFCL locked in a 5% lower circuit and is down about 21% in a month. I did not find a company statement or exchange filing that explains it. Possible factors include selling after the record quarter, a Hold rating from MarketsMOJO on 2 November and weak telecom stocks, but none is confirmed.
 How much has the HFCL share price fallen? 
 Ans. The Univest stock page showed Rs 205.67, down 5.00% from Rs 216.49, on 9 November. Against the 19 October upper circuit price of about Rs 268.81 that is a fall of roughly 23.5% by my arithmetic, so the HFCL lower circuit extends a longer slide. Mint uses a 21% one-month figure, and the bases differ, so check a live quote.
 What were HFCL's Q2 FY27 results, and how did the HFCL share price react? 
 Ans. Consolidated revenue was Rs 2,541.79 crore, up 143.62% year on year, and profit after tax was Rs 394.22 crore, up 448.14%. EBITDA margin was 25.89% against 19.49% a year earlier. The company reported an order book above Rs 28,900 crore, per press reports of the 19 October results.
 What is the HFCL lower circuit limit on the HFCL share price? 
 Ans. The stock trades in the BE series with a 5% daily price band, per MarketsMOJO. That means the price cannot fall or rise more than 5% from the previous close in one session. An exchange can change a band, so check the NSE or BSE circuit list for the current limit.
 Is the HFCL share price expensive after the HFCL lower circuit? 
 Ans. The Univest stock page showed a trailing P/E of about 38.25 and a price to book value of about 5.88 on 9 November, against a P/E near 68.4 around 19 October. The lower P/E mainly reflects a much higher trailing profit. Whether it is expensive depends on whether you believe the profit can be sustained.
 Will the HFCL lower circuit continue? 
 Ans. Nobody can say. The stock has hit lower circuits on several days this month, but it also hit an upper circuit on 4 November. An HFCL lower circuit shows that one side of the market dominated for a session, and they do not predict the next day. Watch volumes, filings and the sector rather than guess.
 What should investors do about the HFCL share price? 
 Ans. Univest does not recommend any security. A holder can check position size, cost price and the company's order execution, while a new buyer can read the Q2 filing and weigh the valuation. Keep in mind that an HFCL lower circuit can block selling, and consult a SEBI-registered adviser for personal advice.
 Where can I check the live HFCL share price? 
 Ans. Use the HFCL Ltd page on Univest, which showed Rs 205.67 on a 9 November snapshot, or the NSE and BSE websites. Prices in this article are time-stamped snapshots from press and data pages, so confirm the latest quote before taking any decision.
